results.title: The AI Compute Price Reset Already Happened
highlights:
AI compute pricing already reset: H100 rental rates rose 40% then fell in July 2026, and Colossus 1 clears $50 million per megawatt of capacity.

...

Anthropic pays SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for a single data center. The building is Colossus 1 in Memphis: more than 300 megawatts of energized capacity and over 220,000 Nvidia GPUs, taken whole, on a contract to May 2029, its terms public through SpaceX's Form FWP. Fifteen billion dollars a year against a 300-megawatt floor puts the ceiling at $50 million per megawatt.

That figure is usually read as a warning that AI compute is about to get more expensive. The warning is late. The repricing has already run: the one-year contract series rose from October 2025 to March 2026, and the spot market peaked in early May 2026. The latest independent reading points the other way: JPMorgan put the average H100 on-demand rental in the non-hyperscale cloud market at $2.68 per GPU-hour in July 2026, down 1.1% on the month and the first decline after seven consecutive increases. It came via a market-news aggregator, not the primary note, and is provisional until that note is in hand.

The durable statement is narrower. The floor under AI compute moved up in late 2025 and is not returning to 2024 levels, the rate of increase is already moderating, and memory constrains supply now while power constrains it from 2027. A 2027 budget built on the 2024 price collapse is priced off the wrong year.

## The Price Rise Everyone Is Quoting Is Real, and the Contract Series Ran From

...

SemiAnalysis maintains an H100 one-year rental price index built from a monthly survey of more than 100 market participants and validated against transaction data. It recorded $1.70 per GPU-hour in October 2025, a break above $2.00 in late January 2026, and $2.35 at the end of March, almost 40% above the October low. Downstream re-reports of those figures all trace back to SemiAnalysis and count as one source.

Three other readings move the same way without sharing that origin. Ornn's live-transaction index put Blackwell spot at $2.75 per GPU-hour in mid-February 2026 and $4.08 by mid-April, a 48% rise. Lambda raised H100 SXM on-demand from $2.99 to $3.99 in June 2026. Verda moved the same card from $2.29 to $3.25 in early 2026. One independent index and two price cards agree on direction.

...

The same GPU carries at least four distinct prices. The published on-demand rate is sticky by design and lags the market. The one-year contract rate is where most volume transacts, the bulk of it in commitments of six months or longer. Spot is the most volatile, and a composite index blends them. Reserved commitments run 20% to 40% below on-demand. Treating a move in one series as a statement about the market is the error underneath most commentary.

### Sold Out Is Not a Figure of Speech: Booked Through September on Half the Providers Surveyed

SemiAnalysis described Blackwell availability as very tight, with capacity arriving through August and September already booked and roughly half of surveyed providers completely sold out. Observed B200 rates in August 2026 span $2.71 to $27.04 per GPU-hour, with GCP's a4-highgpu-8g at $16.11. That is the supply condition every number below sits on.

...

Across the exact window in which the contract rate rose almost 40%, the composite spot-contract index barely moved: $2.84 in October 2025, $2.80 in March 2026, $2.82 in April. Its second-half 2023 peak was $6.62, leaving the composite 57% below the top of the last cycle.

The contract series rose off a distressed floor while the composite still carries spot pricing and legacy contracts rolling down from higher levels. The on-demand range confirms the direction independently, moving from $1.45–$1.95 to $2.10–$2.70 over the same months. On the composite, anyone buying H100 capacity in 2026 pays far less than a buyer in 2023 or 2024.

...

## Then July Happened: The First Monthly Decline in Eight Months

JPMorgan's July 2026 on-demand reading of $2.68 per GPU-hour broke a run of seven consecutive increases. The bank read it as the most strained phase beginning to ease as supply responded, with utilization still above 70%. Ornn places the peak in early May and describes the months since as normalizing. There is precedent: H100 rates fell from roughly $8 an hour to roughly $2 across 2023 and 2024 as supply caught up.

...

Several August 2026 trackers report H100 approaching $3 and B200 at $5.50 to $5.80, up from below $5 in January. JPMorgan and Ornn report a May peak and a decline since. The likeliest reconciliation is that lagging contract and hyperscaler list prices are still ratcheting while non-hyperscale on-demand turned over between May and July. Settling it needs the authoritative series, and the public index page rendered values only through April 2026.

## The $2.60 That Doesn't Exist, and the 52 Weeks That Belong to Memory

The most-quoted number here is an H100 contract rate of $2.60 per GPU-hour in August 2026, from a widely shared chart posted by a paid analyst at Milk Road PRO, a subscription research product that runs published portfolios; Milk Road's public account has urged buying CoreWeave and Nebius. The 40% move and the $1.70 base are correctly taken from SemiAnalysis; the August date and the $2.60 endpoint appear in no source. Use the endpoints that exist: $1.70 in October 2025 to $2.35 in March 2026.

The companion claim, GPU lead times of 36 to 52 weeks, fails the same way. It circulates across at least six 2026 industry analyses and traces to no primary statement from Nvidia, TSMC or any named analyst house. Value Add VC attaches 52 weeks specifically to HBM backlogs, suggesting transposition rather than measurement.

Attributable facts explain the shortage better. TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging is fully allocated, supply-chain analyses report SK Hynix and Micron sold out of their entire 2026 HBM production, and HBM costs rose roughly 30% in the fourth quarter of 2025 alone. Industry analyses put order backlogs near 3.6 million GPUs in April 2026, with demand running 1.4 to 1.6 times supply over 18 to 24 months.

...

The $50 million ceiling holds because frontier-generation clusters are sold whole, under scarcity, to buyers with no alternative. The Google agreement with SpaceX runs at $920 million a month from October 2026 to June 2029 for 110,000 GPUs across more than 100 megawatts, or $71–110 million per megawatt on a floor denominator. None of that describes structurally superior economics. It describes a rent, and a rent that size is collectible only while the input stays scarce.

## The Input That Actually Reprices: PJM Wholesale Power Up 75.5% in a Year

PJM wholesale power averaged $77.78 per megawatt-hour in the first quarter of 2025 and $136.53 in the first quarter of 2026, a rise of 75.5%. The capacity auction cleared 6.8 gigawatts short of the reliability requirement, the third consecutive failure. About $6.3 billion of $16.4 billion in capacity charges for the 2028/29 delivery year is attributable to data-center demand, $29.4 billion across four auctions.

...

### Gartner Said This in November 2024, and the Part Nobody Quotes Is the Price Part

Gartner predicted on 12 November 2024 that power availability would operationally constrain 40% of existing AI data centers by 2027. Bob Johnson, the named VP analyst, argued utility expansion would not keep pace from 2026. The clause almost nobody quotes is the one most on point: Gartner forecast the cost of power itself would rise significantly as operators used their bargaining position to secure supply. A handful of outlets carried one release, and the forecast is now 21 months old.

...

## Power Binds in 2027. Memory Binds Now.

As reported in August 2026, Chamath Palihapitiya argued that power is the single binding constraint on AI compute, ranking hyperscalers above neoclouds above model makers. The fact pattern is sound. The timing is not.

Named principals point elsewhere for 2026. Sam Altman and Brad Lightcap identified memory supply, not power, as the primary bottleneck for training and inference in March 2026. SK Hynix and Micron are sold out of HBM for the year, and TechInsights reports Nvidia designing newer inference silicon around HBM limits. The constraints bind on different clocks: memory determines how many GPUs ship in 2026, power how much capacity can exist from 2027.

...

Man Group, an institutional asset manager with its own positions in the trade, argues that power infrastructure built for 2024 and 2025 demand risks becoming stranded by 2027 and 2028, with a first wave of defaults as initial lease terms renew. CoreWeave's 49 data centers are essentially all leased from third parties, the silicon depreciates on a four-to-six-year clock, and the debt behind it frequently outlasts the contracts it was underwritten against.

...

The spread across procurement modes is wider than the spread across time. Hyperscaler on-demand H100 runs $3.90 to $12.29 per GPU-hour, with AWS at the top of that range and GCP between $9 and $11.50. CoreWeave reserved runs about $2.06 to $2.49, specialist marketplaces $1.49 to $2.69. Reserved sits 20% to 40% under on-demand, Verda spot 65% to 70% under. The observed 2026 shift is hybrid: a reserved baseline, spot for spikes.

...

### Your Real Problem Is Probably 5% Utilization, Not a 40% Rate Move

An unnamed 2026 industry report puts average enterprise GPU utilization near 5%, driven by over-provisioning and inefficient scheduling. That figure traces to no named publisher and should be read as directionally right and specifically soft. Better established, though the sourcing is FinOps-vendor-adjacent: inference takes roughly 85% of enterprise AI budgets, most teams find spend running two to three times expectation, and agentic workloads consume 5 to 30 times more tokens per task than a chatbot call. A buyer at single-digit utilization overpays by an order of magnitude whatever the rate.

### Match Contract Duration to Workload Certainty, Not to Price Fear

Locking three years of capacity at a cyclical peak, into a market with a credible 2027 oversupply scenario and hardware that obsoletes in four to six years, is its own way to get hurt. So is budgeting on continued deflation. Neither is solved by predicting the price. Both are solved by matching contract duration to workload certainty and splitting a reserved baseline from burst capacity.

...

The era of AI compute as a deflating commodity ended in late 2025. What followed was a cyclical upswing off a distressed trough, layered on a multi-year decline that has not reversed, and it is already moderating. Memory binds now, power from 2027, and the largest buyers are exiting the rental market by building their own.

$50 million per megawatt caps what the scarcest input in this industry is worth to a buyer with no alternative. The operators who get hurt over the next two years, the 2027 and 2028 window Man Group flags, will be those who budgeted for continued deflation, or who locked multi-year capacity at the top of a spike and then ran it at 5% utilization. Neither mistake requires a price forecast to avoid.

results.title: AI算力需求帶動硬體漲價潮 陸3C產品租賃訂單翻倍 - 日報 - 工商時報
highlights:
- 2026.08.10
- 03:00
- 工商時報 葉聖平 

人工智慧算力需求提高記憶體成本，並帶動3C硬體漲價潮。其中，蘋果及安卓陣營產品調價，直接刺激大陸3C產品租賃市場。陸媒引述業者指出，電腦、高階手機及相機租賃訂單明顯增加，部分產品年增甚至達數倍至20倍，但同時面臨設備採購成本增加與缺貨問題。

科創板日報報導，大陸知名3C租賃平台「惠租」負責人表示，7月的電腦租賃訂單，合計超過2萬台，較上個月成長20％，與去年同期相比大增115％。除了傳統辦公與遊戲需求外，今年愈來愈多消費者因人工智慧應用轉向租用高效能設備。

此外，暑假、旅遊及演唱會需求，也同步帶動租賃市場。7月演唱會手機租賃超過4萬台，月增75％。

另一家3C租賃平台「樂小租」執行長趙錦鵬表示，受記憶體漲價影響，7月電腦租賃訂單量增加50％，不過租賃價格僅調升5％。

他分析，高階電腦售價上升，使部分消費者轉向租賃替代購買，然而設備成本同步增加，也使租賃業者的電腦採購量至少下降50％，不敢大幅補貨。

租賃需求翻倍的原因，在於AI持續拉動高頻寬記憶體（HBM）及動態隨機存取記憶體（DRAM）需求，記憶體廠將更多產能轉向高附加價值的人工智慧產品，使得消費電子用記憶體供應受到排擠。

調研機構TrendForce預估，2026年第三季傳統DRAM合約價，將季增13％至18％；快閃記憶體（NAND Flash）合約價，將季增10％至15％，其中，電腦常見的暫存記憶體DDR4 8GB，於7月平均合約價升至24美元，月增14.3％。

報導指出，與第二季相比，第三季預估漲幅已縮小，但人工智慧伺服器與高頻寬記憶體需求擴張、排擠記憶體產能的局面在短期內難以改變。

results.title: AI Inference Token Costs Fall 37.5% as GPU Rental Fees Rise 15.2%, Power Crunch Extends Infrastructure Timeline to 5-10 Years | Gate News
highlights: According to Citi analyst Heath Terry's latest AI industry tracker, inference token costs have fallen 37.5% from May peaks to $1.33 per million tokens in Q2, while Blackwell GPU rental fees rose 15.2% to $5.18 per hour. This divergence reflects intelligent routing systems that automatically assign models by task complexity, lowering costs systematically. However, power constraints, licensing delays, and labor shortages have lengthened infrastructure production capacity expansion from an initial 3-year timeline to 5-10 years. Data centers now account for approximately 90% of new power grid applications.

results.title: Broad Conviction in a Narrow Market – AdvisorAnalyst.com
highlights:
The catalyst was Anthropic. On February 5th, the release of Claude Opus 4.6 transformed the company's commercial trajectory, turning it into what Ryan describes as "the leading AI lab." What followed was a cascade: massive fundraising rounds, a disclosed annualized revenue run-rate of $47 billion (roughly five times the start-of-year figure), and a tenfold increase in contracted compute commitments. That surge in demand collided with an already tight market for AI hardware. GPU rental prices, which ordinarily decline as hardware generations age, moved sharply higher instead.

Memory chips became the defining bottleneck. The three major suppliers of high-bandwidth memory, Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix, more than doubled prices per unit and saw combined profits increase nearly tenfold to $96 billion in a single quarter. Ryan puts this in sharp context: the top five AI hyperscalers spent roughly $150 billion on capital expenditure in the same period. "Pure price increases from memory companies," he notes, "are now consuming a large amount of the total spend, a factor that will necessarily force returns on investment lower."

...

There is also a demand-side question that Ryan raises with evident care. Near-term demand may have been temporarily inflated by what he calls "Claude-fever" — corporate enthusiasm to experiment with powerful models, sometimes without fully appreciating deployment costs at scale. In one notable case, a company reportedly spent $500 million on Claude in a single month. Uber consumed its entire annual AI budget within months of the year starting. "While long-term demand seems likely to be enormous," Ryan observes, "supply could still outpace near-term adoption as implementation becomes the next bottleneck."

...

1. Concentration in AI is a risk, not just an opportunity. Semiconductor volatility near all-time highs has historically preceded drawdowns, not recoveries.

...

Memory chips are the canary. ... Margin compression for the largest AI buyers is already underway.

...

4. ... With energy equities already pricing in lower oil and Strait of Hormuz disruptions still unresolved, the asymmetry favors continued exposure, particularly given its diversification value relative to both equities and fixed income.

...

Diversification across uncorrelated positions is outperforming quiet conformity.

results.title: AI 基本面与市场定价的背离：GPU 租赁、现金流与算力供给的证据链 - 天机亘古
highlights:
- 2026 年年中 AI 板块经历显著回调，但硅谷投资人 Gavin Baker（Atreides Management 创始人）在近期公开访谈中提出：经过对供应链、算力现货价格、Token 调用量等量化指标的系统梳理，未发现任何一项正在恶化的基本面指标，估值与基本面之间存在明显背离。
- 存量 GPU 租赁价格逆势上行是其论证的核心证据。据访谈援引的市场数据，B200 集群租赁价格七个月内由每小时约 2 美元升至约 4 美元；Baker 在公开渠道亦指出，GPU 算力现货价格已达到长期合约价格的两倍以上。
- Baker 主张以经营现金流（operating cash flow）而非自由现金流（free cash flow）评估超大规模云厂商的财务健康度，并认为开源模型的兴起转移的是模型层利润分配，而非算力总需求。
- 该访谈同时提示了两项非共识风险：其一，投资者普遍借助大语言模型解读新闻，导致市场观点同质化、交易周期被大幅压缩；其二，行业最大的外部风险来自监管与社会接受度，而非技术本身。
- Baker 给出了三条明确的证伪条件：云厂商经营现金流停止加速、GPU 价格持续下行、主要模型公司 Token 总量停滞且开源未能扩大总盘。截至访谈发布时点，上述条件均未出现。

...

### 2.1 存量 GPU 租赁价格逆势上行

针对市场回调，Baker 的调研方法是直接寻找反面证据：在硅谷范围内征询各方，要求对方指出哪怕一项正在恶化的量化指标。据其陈述，该调研未获得有效反例——供应链、现货价格、Token 调用量等指标不仅未恶化，多数仍在加速改善。

其中最具张力的数据来自 GPU 租赁市场。行业此前的主流预期是，随着新一代芯片投放，存量 GPU 租金将逐步回落乃至崩塌；但据访谈援引的报价，已投入使用两至三年的存量卡价格在 2026 年仍在上行，B200 集群租赁价格七个月内由每小时约 2 美元升至约 4 美元，且有机构预计下一代 Blackwell 产品的租赁价格可能接近翻倍。Baker 在其公开渠道进一步指出，GPU 算力现货价格已实质性高于长期合约价格，幅度在两倍以上。

该现象的财务含义在于合约重定价周期。算力租赁公司在融资约束下普遍以长期合约锁定收入，当前大量算力仍按显著低于现货价的旧约执行；随着合同陆续到期重签，相关公司的收入存在阶梯式上调空间。据此，Baker 提出其核心反问：若核心产品仍在涨价，则“利润是虚增的”这一市场定价假设难以成立。

...

其主张的替代指标是经营现金流。据访谈援引的数据，微软、Meta、亚马逊三家合计经营现金流增速已由 28% 提升至 32%；考虑到新一代 GPU 尚未大规模投产、存量合约尚未重定价，该加速趋势具备延续基础。

...

其一是 Meta 宣布对外出租算力。市场将其解读为产能过剩、资本开支即将收缩的信号，但随后的财报未显示开支削减。Baker 给出的解释是：Meta 观察到 SpaceX 以显著高于长期合约价的水平对外出售大型训练集群算力，意识到自有算力存在同类变现空间，故选择出租。换言之，这是稀缺资源的高价变现行为，而非过剩库存的出清行为。

...

### 2.7 需求渗透率与供给缺口

Baker 判断 AI 需求的爆发期尚未开始。据其测算，当前全球能够实际使用代理式 AI（agentic AI）完成工作的用户约为 25 万至 50 万人，不足全球人口的 0.01%。在用户规模向亿级迈进的过程中，算力系统更可能维持供给短缺状态，而非转入过剩。

...

区别于多数看多论述，Baker 明确给出了推翻自身判断的三项条件：

1. 超大规模云厂商经营现金流增速停止加速，乃至转为恶化；
2. GPU 价格持续崩塌，算力供给普遍过剩；
3. 所有主要模型公司的 Token 总量停滞或下降，且开源生态未能扩大调用总盘。

据其陈述，截至访谈发布时点，三项条件无一出现。其方法论立场可概括为访谈中的原句：“未来永远是一个概率分布，不是一个确定性的答案。”在其框架下，投资研究的任务不是无条件看多，而是持续寻找能够推翻自身判断的事实；当存量 GPU 租金上行、模型调用加速、经营现金流改善时，不应因股价下跌而假定基本面已经转坏。

results.title: RTX 5090 임대 시장은 AI 컴퓨팅 위기가 오직 상위권에서만 실제로 존재한다는 것을 증명합니다.
highlights:
GPU 임대 시장은 두 부분으로 나뉘어 있습니다. 어떤 부분에 속해 있는지 파악하는 것이, 과도한 비용을 지불해야 하는지, 아니면 이익을 얻을 수 있는지 결정하는 요소입니다.

올해 내내 AI 컴퓨팅 관련 뉴스를 주의 깊게 살펴보셨다면, 핵심은 간단합니다. GPU의 공급이 제한적이며, 가격도 상승하고 있습니다. 하지만 그건 H100, B200, B300과 같은 GPU를 임대하는 경우에 해당합니다. RTX 5090의 임대 시장은 전혀 다른 상황입니다. 대부분의 투자자와 분석가들은 소비자용 GPU는 “진지한 AI 인프라”가 아니기 때문에 이를 별로 중요하게 여기지 않습니다.

...

### 가격 정보는 부족한 상황이라는 주장을 뒷받침하지 않습니다. 소비자 단계에서 말이죠.

2026년 8월 기준으로, RTX 5090은 최소한의 비용으로 임대할 수 있습니다. Vast.ai에서, $0.27/시간살라드의 분산 네트워크에서의 평균값입니다.$0.50/시간 7개 제공업체의 123개 온디맨드 상품을 포함합니다. 다양한 제공업체를 통한 중간값은$0.56/시간 0.27달러에서 1.05달러까지의 범위입니다. 이는 희귀한 자산의 가격이 아닙니다.

온디맨드 RTX 5090 대여 가격은약 43%가 떨어졌습니다. 2025년 4월부터 시간당 요금이 0.89달러에서 0.51달러로 감소했습니다. 한편, 67개 공급업체와 17개 GPU 모델을 바탕으로 구성된 AIMultiple GPU 지수에 따르면 RTX 5090의 가용성이 높아졌습니다. 75–77%가 확인된 재고 수량 H100s보다 훨씬 높은 수치입니다(48–53%), B200s는 28–38%, B300s는 17–20%입니다.

소비자용 GPU 시장은 과잉 상태입니다. 공급이 너무 많습니다.

공급원이 그 이유를 설명해줍니다. SaladCloud만이 분산된 네트워크를 운영합니다. 45만 명 이상의 GPU 소유자하루에 20,000개 이상의 활성화된 GPU가 사용되고 있습니다. RTX 5090s는 CES가 시작된 지 24시간 만에 그들의 플랫폼에 도입되었습니다. 이 장비들은 이탈리아, 미국, 영국의 개별 하드웨어 소유자들이 공급한 것입니다. NVIDIA의 공급망이나 데이터센터 구매와는 관련이 없습니다. 단지 수백 개의 GPU가 일주일 안에 시장에 출시된 것일 뿐입니다. 이는 공급망의 문제가 아니라, 수천 명의 개인들이 소비자용 GPU를 구매하여 그 여분의 컴퓨팅 자원을 다시 시장에 제공하는 현상입니다.

### 문제점: 데이터센터용 GPU는 두 배로 증가했지만, 소비자용 GPU는 반으로 줄었습니다.

RTX 5090의 임대 가격 하락은 우연한 일이 아니었습니다. 이는 극도로 치열한 시장에서 불가능할 것 같은 상황과 함께 일어난 것입니다. 즉, 데이터센터용 GPU의 임대 가격이 상당히 낮아진 것입니다.지난 한 해 동안 두 배로 증가했습니다. H100의 1년 계약 가격은 시간당 1.70달러에서 약 2.35달러로 상승했습니다. B200의 현물 환율은 시간당 2.75달러에서 5.64달러로 급등했습니다. B300의 경우 시간당 평균 8.23달러입니다.

이 메커니즘은 물리적인 것입니다. TSMC의 CoWoS 패키징 능력은 2027년 중반까지 모두 가득 찼습니다. HBM3e 메모리의 가격은 2026년 계약에 있어서 약 20% 상승했습니다. 이는 삼성, SK Hynix, Micron이 DDR5에서 고대역폭 메모리로 웨이버 공간을 재배정했기 때문입니다. AI 데이터 센터는 전 세계 DRAM 생산량의 약 40%를 차지합니다. NVIDIA는 데이터 센터용 제품을 우선적으로 생산하기 위해 2026년 상반기에 RTX 50시리즈 제품의 생산량을 30~40% 줄였습니다.

결과는 다음과 같습니다: RTX 5090의 가격이 공식 출시 가격인 1,999달러에서 급격히 상승한 것과 같은 메모리 부족 문제가 발생했습니다.소매가로 4,300달러–5,100달러또한, 데이터센터의 공급망도 고갈되었습니다. 하지만 RTX 5090의 임대 시장은 데이터센터의 공급망에 의해 제한되지 않습니다. 이 시장에는 이미 공장을 떠난 카드들이 존재하며, 소매 채널을 거쳐 개인의 지하실이나 가정용 서버에 설치된 카드들도 있습니다.

AI 컴퓨팅 작업은 실제로 일어나고 있어요. 다만 살라드 네트워크에 있는 450,000명의 GPU 소유자들까지는 포함되지 않아요.

...

이곳에서 임대 가격을 통해 NVIDIA가 원하지 않는 총 소유 비용에 대한 결론이 나오게 됩니다.

현재 소매 시장에서 RTX 5090의 가격은 4,300달러에서 5,100달러 사이입니다. 만약 이 제품을 구입하여 시간당 0.21달러라는 가장 저렴한 임대료로 사용한다면, 약 8,500시간에서 24,300시간 동안의 수익이 발생합니다. 이는 354일에서 1,012일에 해당하는 시간이며, 전력, 호스팅, 유지보수 비용이 전혀 없다고 가정했을 때의 수치입니다. 더 현실적인 수치로, 시간당 0.36달러의 평균 임대료를 고려하면, 6,000시간에서 14,200시간 정도의 수익이 발생합니다.

어떤 소비자 하드웨어 소유자도 100%의 활용률을 달성할 수 없습니다. 어떤 홈용 장치도 전력과 전원 공급 비용을 회수할 수 없습니다. 3× RTX 5090 시스템에는 3개의 2,000W 전원 공급 장치가 필요합니다. RTX 5090의 구매 대비 임대 비용 측면에서는 결정적인 변화가 일어났습니다. 이는 간헐적 사용자들뿐만 아니라, 1년 전에 구매하려고 했던 사람들에게도 해당됩니다.

그것은 중요합니다. 왜냐하면 NVIDIA의 전체 소비자용 GPU 사업은 구매자가 하드웨어 비용을 부담하는 데 달려 있기 때문입니다. 반면 임대 시장에서는 전기와 대역폭의 단순한 비용만을 반영하여 매분당 4센트로 카드를 임대하는 방식이므로, 자본 지출 모델은 무너지게 됩니다.

NVIDIA는 자신이 가격을 결정할 수 있는 분야에서 공급 부족을 유발하고 있습니다. 반면 소비자층은 분산된 네트워크를 통해 자사의 경제적 원칙을 완전히 무시함으로써 상품화가 이루어집니다.

...

단순히 임대 비용 경제학만으로는 설득력이 부족하다면, 1달러당 인식 성능을 고려하면 충분하다. 2026년 3월에 스페론의 경우 시간당 0.76달러로, RTX 5090은 약 Llama 3.1 8B 모델의 경우, FP16 방식으로 초당 3,500 토큰입니다.대략적으로는 그렇습니다.백만 토큰당 0.060달러 H100 PCIe를 시간당 2.01달러에 사용하면 약 5,000토큰을 초당 생성할 수 있습니다. 이는 더 빠른 속도이지만, 시간당 비용은 2.6배 증가함으로써 처리량은 43%만 증가합니다.

results.title: Global GPU Computing News【20260809】 - Cloud GPU Rental Platform-Focused on Bulk Supply and Cost-effective AI GPU Rental Service
highlights:
1. China’s first fully domestically produced 100,000‑GPU AI supercluster goes live The National Development and Reform Commission announced that the country’s first domestically made AI supercluster with 100,000 GPUs was officially put into operation this week, marking a new stage in large‑scale deployment. Multiple computing nodes across the country have also been expanded accordingly.
2. Moore Threads reports 147.42% year‑on‑year revenue growth in H1 2026 On August 9, Chinese GPU maker Moore Threads released its semi‑annual report for 2026, posting revenue of RMB 1.736 billion in the first half, up 147.42% year‑on‑year and already exceeding its full‑year 2025 revenue. Net loss attributable to parent company narrowed by 95.73%. The same day, the company announced it is preparing for an H‑share listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, pursuing a dual “A+H” platform.
3. AMD launches Instinct MI455X flagship AI GPU At its “Advancing AI 2026” event, AMD unveiled the Instinct MI455X accelerator, featuring 320 billion transistors, 432GB of HBM4 memory, and FP4 compute of 40 PFLOPS, with certain specs surpassing NVIDIA’s Rubin architecture. It also introduced the Helios rack‑scale platform, integrating 72 GPUs to deliver up to 2.9 EFLOPS of compute power.
4. NVIDIA mulls cutting Rubin Ultra memory to ease HBM shortage Industry media reported on August 6 that NVIDIA is considering reducing the HBM capacity of its next‑gen Rubin Ultra GPU from the originally planned ~384GB to 192GB, a nearly 50% cut, while also reducing the number of GPU chiplets from four to two, in order to alleviate tight supply of advanced HBM.
5. SpaceX partners with NVIDIA to send data‑center‑grade computing into space On August 5, SpaceX announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to develop the Starmind AI1 satellite compute payload, with each satellite equipped with an NVIDIA Rubin GPU and Vera CPU, enabling data‑center‑class computing capabilities in space.
6. Meta launches GPU rental business Meta officially announced on August 5 that it is commercialising its compute capacity by starting to rent out its own GPU resources to external customers, shifting its role from a major global purchaser of compute to a supplier, creating business‑level competition with NVIDIA.
7. Rental prices for NVIDIA H100 and B200 GPUs rise Latest industry data show that hourly rental rates for NVIDIA H100 GPUs have increased by about 50% since January this year, from under $2 to nearly $3; B200 rental prices are also moving up, reflecting continued tight supply‑demand balance in the compute market.
8. Intel Arc Pro B70 adapts MiniMax H3 video model on day zero On August 3, Intel announced that its Arc Pro B70 GPU has achieved day‑zero adaptation for the open‑source multimodal video model MiniMax H3. The card is based on the second‑gen Xe2 architecture, with 32 Xe cores and 32GB of GDDR6 memory, delivering peak AI compute of 367 TOPS.
9. Nine global cloud giants significantly raise capex guidance Major cloud providers have recently released Q2 earnings and revised up their full‑year capital expenditure guidance. TrendForce projects that the combined capex of the top nine cloud vendors will exceed $886.7 billion in 2026, up nearly 90% year‑on‑year; the annual growth forecast for AI server shipments has been raised to nearly 31%.
10. China’s domestic GPU rental quotes remain generally stable Data as of August 6 show that among six domestic GPU rental quotes, four were flat, one rose, and one fell. The A800‑80G increased by 6.86%, while the RTX 5090‑32G decreased by 2.08%; the other four remained unchanged, indicating overall stable pricing.
